title: Ribbons and pearls
caption: Barred spiral galaxy NGC 1398, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 1398 · constellation Fornax · about 65 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Ribbons of gas and dust wrap around a pearly center in this view of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1398. Dark lanes of dust mottle its spiral arms, and pink-hued star-forming regions are scattered through its outer parts. The galaxy lies about 65 million light-years away in the constellation of Fornax, the Furnace.

Its arms do not begin at the very center and swirl outward. Instead they stem from a straight bar of stars that cuts across the galaxy's middle. Around two thirds of spiral galaxies are seen to have such a bar, yet astronomers still aren't sure whether, or how, bars shape the way a galaxy behaves and develops.
The data come from FORS2, an instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile, which recorded the galaxy in fine detail.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.17 x 7.27 arcminutes) and distance (65 million light years), the frame spans roughly 136,000 × 137,000 light-years. Its light set out about 65 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a visible-light image from the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, using B, V and R filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter that traces glowing hydrogen. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
filters: 440 nm · Optical B (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
557 nm · Optical V (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
655 nm · Optical R (Very Large Telescope FORS2)

understand.eye: The long exposure collects far more light than the eye can, revealing faint dust lanes and pink star-forming regions that would not be visible by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture was made for ESO's Cosmic Gems program, an outreach effort that photographs interesting or attractive objects using telescope time that cannot be used for science. The data still go into ESO's science archive, where astronomers can use them.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with a pale bright center and curving arms marked by dark dust lanes and pink patches.
